<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; In the past we have entered into, and may in the future enter into, certain derivative arrangements with respect to portions of our natural gas and crude oil production, to reduce our sensitivity to volatile commodity prices, and with respect to portions of our debt, to reduce our sensitivity to volatile interest rates.&#160;&#160;None of our derivative instruments are designated as cash flow or fair value hedges.&#160;&#160;We believe that these derivative arrangements, although not free of risk, allow us to achieve a more predictable cash flow and to reduce exposure to commodity price and interest rate fluctuations.&#160;&#160;However, derivative arrangements limit the benefit of increases in the prices of natural gas, crude oil and natural gas liquids sales and limit the benefit of decreases in interest rates.&#160;&#160;Moreover, our derivative arrangements apply only to a portion of our production and our debt and provide only partial protection against declines in commodity prices and increases in interest rates, respectively.&#160;&#160;Such arrangements may expose us to risk of financial loss in certain circumstances.&#160;&#160;We continuously reevaluate our hedging programs in light of changes in production, market conditions, commodity price forecasts, capital spending, interest rate forecasts and debt service requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; We use a mix of commodity swaps, put options, costless collars and interest rate swaps to accomplish our hedging strategy.&#160;&#160;Derivative assets and liabilities with the same counterparty, subject to contractual terms which provide for net settlement, are reported on a net basis on our consolidated balance sheets.&#160;&#160;We have exposure to financial institutions in the form of derivative transactions in connection with our hedges.&#160;&#160;These transactions are with counterparties in the financial services industry, and specifically with members of our bank group.&#160;&#160;These transactions could expose us to credit risk in the event of default of our counterparties.&#160;&#160;We believe our counterparty risk is low in part because of the offsetting relationship we have with each of our counterparties provided for in our revolving credit agreement and various hedge contracts.&#160;&#160;See Note&#160;5 - &#8220;Fair Value Measurements&#8221; for further information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">F-16</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Debt</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revolving Credit Agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On May&#160;8, 2007, we entered into a $400.0&#160;million revolving credit agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (&#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Wells Fargo Bank</font>&#8221;), as agent, and the lender parties thereto (the &#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Senior Credit Agreement</font>&#8221;) dated as of July&#160;15, 2005, as amended.&#160;&#160;Since that time, we have amended and restated this agreement as necessary.&#160;&#160;Our Senior Credit Agreement provides for aggregate borrowings of up to $400.0&#160;million for acquisitions of crude oil and gas properties and for general corporate cash requirements.&#160;&#160;The Senior Credit Agreement includes usual and customary covenants for credit facilities of the respective types and sizes, including, among others, limitations on liens, hedging, mergers, asset sales or dispositions, payments of dividends, incurrence of additional indebtedness, certain leases and investments outside of the ordinary course of business, as well as events of default.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Senior Credit Agreement contains certain financial covenants, including those currently requiring us to maintain (i)&#160;a ratio of current assets (including borrowing base availability and excluding derivative instruments) to current liabilities (excluding current portion of long-term debt and derivative instruments) of at least 1.0 to 1.0, (ii)&#160;the ratio of our total debt to Adjusted EBITDAX for any four trailing fiscal quarters which may not be greater than (a)&#160;4.25 to 1.00 as of the end of any fiscal quarter through June&#160;30, 2011, (b)&#160;3.75 to 1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending September&#160;30, 2011 and December&#160;31, 2011, and (c)&#160;3.50 to 1.00 thereafter, (iii)&#160;the ratio of Adjusted EBITDAX to cash interest expense for any four trailing fiscal quarters may not be less than (a)&#160;2.00 through March&#160;31, 2011, (b)&#160;2.25 to 1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending June&#160;30, 2011, September&#160;30, 2011 and December&#160;31, 2011, and (c)&#160;2.50 to 1.00 for the quarters ending March&#160;31, 2012 and June&#160;30, 2012 and (d)&#160;2.75 to 1.00 thereafter, and (iv)&#160;the ratio of the sum of (a)&#160;the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Loans under the revolver plus (b)&#160;the aggregate face amount of all undrawn and uncancelled Letters of Credit, plus the aggregate of all amounts drawn under all Letters of Credit and not yet reimbursed, as of such date to EBITDAX for the four fiscal quarters ending on such date to not be greater than 2.25 to 1.00.&#160;&#160;EBITDAX represents net income (loss) before net interest expense, taxes, and depreciation, amortization and exploration expenses.&#160;&#160;Adjusted EBITDAX, as defined in our credit agreements, represents EBITDAX as further adjusted for (i)&#160;unrealized gain or loss on derivative instruments, (ii)&#160;non-cash share-based compensation charges, (iii)&#160;impaired assets, (iv)&#160;other financing costs and (v)&#160;gains or losses on the disposition of assets, all of which will be required in determining our compliance with financial covenants under our Senior Credit Agreement and second lien term loan agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Borrowings under our Senior Credit Agreement are subject to a borrowing base limitation based on our proved crude oil and natural gas reserves.&#160;&#160;The borrowing base under our Senior Credit Agreement is currently $100.0&#160;million. The next borrowing base re-determination is scheduled for May&#160;1, 2012 and is subject to semi-annual redeterminations, although our lenders may elect to make one additional redetermination between scheduled redetermination dates.&#160;&#160;We may also issue up to $200&#160;million in senior unsecured notes.&#160;&#160;Any such issuance of senior unsecured notes will reduce our borrowing base by 25% of the net proceeds from such issuance in excess of $150&#160;million.&#160;&#160;Our Senior Credit Agreement also provides for the issuance of letters-of-credit up to a $5.0&#160;million sub-limit.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, no senior unsecured notes or letters-of-credit were outstanding.&#160;&#160;All principal amounts, together with all accrued and unpaid interest outstanding under our Senior Credit Agreement will be due and payable in full on May&#160;31, 2013.&#160;&#160;We have started discussions with Wells Fargo Bank to extend our Senior Credit Agreement and expect to finalize these discussions before the debt becomes current on May 31, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Advances under our Senior Credit Agreement are in the form of either base rate loans or LIBOR loans.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the base rate loans fluctuates based upon the higher of the lender&#8217;s &#8220;prime rate&#8221; and the Federal Funds rate.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the LIBOR loans fluctuates based upon the rate at which Eurodollar deposits in the LIBOR market are quoted for the maturity selected.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to our Senior Credit Agreement, the applicable margin is between 2.75% and 3.50%, for LIBOR loans, and between 1.50% and 2.00%, for base rate loans.&#160;&#160;The specific interest margin applicable is determined by, in each case, the percent of the borrowing base utilized at the time of the credit extension.&#160;&#160;LIBOR loans of one, two, three and six months may be selected.&#160;&#160;The commitment fee payable on the unused portion of our borrowing base is 0.50%, which fee accrues and is payable quarterly in arrears.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2011, we had $21.0&#160;million outstanding under our Senior Credit Agreement, with availability of $79.0&#160;million.</font></div>

<br>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Second Lien Credit Agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We entered into a new second lien credit agreement with Barclays Bank Plc, as agent, and the lender parties thereto, including an affiliate of OCM GW Holdings, LLC (&#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Oaktree Holdings</font>&#8221;), our largest stockholder (the &#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Second Lien Credit Agreement</font>&#8221;) which provided for term loans, made to us in a single draw, in an aggregate principal amount of $175&#160;million on December&#160;27, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our Second Lien Credit Agreement replaced our then existing $150&#160;million Second Lien Credit Agreement with Credit Suisse, which was paid off in full and terminated at closing.&#160;&#160;Our Second Lien Credit Agreement matures on December&#160;27, 2015.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Advances under our new Second Lien Credit Agreement are in the form of either base rate loans or LIBOR loans.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the base rate loans fluctuates based upon the greatest of (i)&#160;4.00% per annum, (ii)&#160;the &#8220;prime rate&#8221;, (iii)&#160;the Federal Funds Effective Rate plus &#189; of 1% and (iv)&#160;the LIBO rate for a one month interest period plus 1.00%.&#160;&#160;The applicable margin for base rate loans is 8.50%.&#160;&#160;The interest rate on the LIBOR loans fluctuates based upon the higher of (i)&#160;3.0% per annum and (ii)&#160;the LIBOR rate per annum.&#160;&#160;The applicable margin for LIBOR loans is 9.50%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to certain of the Senior Credit Agreement covenants described above, the Second Lien Credit Agreement also requires the ratio of PV-10 Value to total Net Debt to be greater than 1.25 to 1.00 as of the end of the second and fourth calendar quarters through June&#160;30, 2012 and 1.50 to 1.00 thereafter.&#160;&#160;The PV-10 Value represents the present value of estimated future revenues less severance and ad valorem taxes, operating, gathering, transportation and marketing expenses and capital expenditures from the production of proved reserves on our oil and gas properties as set forth in the most recent reserve reports.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, we had a principal amount of $175.0&#160;million outstanding under our Second Lien Credit Agreement, with a discount of $5.9&#160;million using the estimated market value interest rate at the time of issuance, for a net balance of $169.1&#160;million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Summary</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2011, we were in compliance with the covenants under our Senior Credit Agreement and Second Lien Credit Agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Senior Credit Agreement and our Second Lien Credit Agreement are secured by liens on substantially all of our assets, including the capital stock of our subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;The liens securing the obligations under our Second Lien Credit Agreement are junior to those under our Senior Credit Agreement.&#160;&#160;Unpaid interest is payable under our credit agreements as borrowings mature and renew.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our debt consists of the following:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">our predecessors-in-interest through the acquisition documents relating to the acquisition of our interest in these wells.&#160;&#160;The damages currently alleged are approximately $13.4&#160;million.&#160;&#160;We and our co-defendants are vigorously defending this lawsuit and we believe that we have meritorious defenses.&#160;&#160;We do not believe this suit will have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position, results of operations or cash flows, although we cannot guarantee that a material adverse effect will not occur.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2010, we and several predecessor operators were named in a lawsuit filed by an entity alleging that it owns a working interest in a productive formation that has not been recognized by us or by predecessor operators to which we have granted indemnification rights.&#160;&#160;In dispute is whether ownership rights in specific depths were transferred through a number of decade-old poorly documented transactions.&#160;&#160;The maximum amount asserted in the suit filed could be determined at up to approximately $4.9&#160;million.&#160;&#160;We are vigorously defending this lawsuit and believe we have meritorious defenses.&#160;&#160;We currently do not believe that this claim will have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position, results of operations or cash flows, although we cannot guarantee that a material adverse effect will not occur.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Employment Agreements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2011, we entered into amended and restated employment agreements with our President/Chief Executive Officer and Senior Vice President/Chief Financial Officer.&#160;&#160;Each agreement has a term of three years with automatic yearly extensions unless we or the executive officer elects not to extend the agreement.&#160;&#160;These agreements provide for an annual base salary of $450,000 and $365,000, respectively, subject to increases at the discretion of the Compensation Committee.&#160;&#160;If the contracts are terminated by us without cause or by the employee for good reason, and the employee has been in compliance with employee contract terms, the employee may receive a cash payment equal to 2.99&#160;times the sum of the current calendar year&#8217;s base salary plus prior year&#8217;s annual cash incentive bonus, health insurance benefits for 36 months and acceleration to 100% vested status for all stock, stock option and other equity awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Also in June 2011, we entered into amended and restated employment agreements with two other Senior Vice Presidents.&#160;&#160;Each agreement has a term of two years with automatic yearly extensions unless we or the executive officer elects not to extend the agreement.&#160;&#160;These agreements provide for an annual base salary ranging from $220,000 to $230,000, subject to increases at the discretion of the Compensation Committee.&#160;&#160;If the contracts are terminated by us without cause or by the employee for good reason, and the employee has been in compliance with the employee contract terms, the employee is entitled to receive a cash payment equal to two times current year base salary plus prior year&#8217;s annual cash incentive bonus, health insurance benefits for 24&#160;months and acceleration to 100% vested status for all stock, stock option and other equity awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In May 2010, we entered into an employment agreement with a new Senior Vice President.&#160;&#160;This agreement has a term of two years with automatic yearly extensions unless we or the executive officer elects not to extend the agreement.&#160;&#160;This agreement provides for an initial base salary of $230,000&#160;per year, subject to increases at the discretion of the Compensation Committee.&#160;&#160;If the contracts are terminated by us without cause or by the employee for good reason, and the employee has been in compliance with the employee contract terms, the employee is entitled to receive a cash payment equal to two times current year base salary plus prior year&#8217;s annual cash incentive bonus, health insurance benefits for 24&#160;months and acceleration to 100% vested status for all stock, stock option and other equity awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 36pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">11.</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Share-Based Compensation</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, we had share-based compensation, which includes both stock options and restricted stock awarded to employees and directors that were either performance related or granted upon initial employment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Incentive Plans</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the third quarter 2008, our Board of Directors formally adopted an amendment to our performance based cash bonus plan and adopted a new performance based long term stock bonus plan for the benefit of all employees - the Crimson Cash Incentive Bonus Plan (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;CIBP&#8221;</font>) and the Crimson Long-Term Incentive Plan (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;LTIP&#8221;</font>), respectively.&#160;&#160;Both plans and specific targeted performance measures under those plans, were approved by the Compensation Committee.&#160;&#160;Upon achieving the performance levels established each year, bonus awards were </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">F-20</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">calculated as a percentage of base salary for the plan year.&#160;&#160;The plan awards were disbursed in the first quarter of the following year.&#160;&#160;Employees must have been employed by us at the time that final plan awards were dispersed to have been eligible.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The CIBP awards are paid out in cash (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Cash Awards&#8221;</font>).&#160;&#160;The performance targets were evaluated on a quarterly basis and used to estimate the approximate expense earned to date for each year.&#160;&#160;The Board of Directors suspended the CIBP for 2009.&#160;&#160;However, discretionary cash bonus awards of approximately $1.2&#160;million were approved by the Board of Directors for fiscal year 2009 and were paid in March 2010.&#160;&#160;The CIBP was reinstated by the Board of Directors for fiscal year 2010.&#160;&#160;Approximately $2.8&#160;million and $2.9&#160;million was recognized as compensation expense related to the Cash Awards for the twelve months ended December&#160;31, 2011 and 2010, respectively and were paid in March 2012 and 2011, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The LTIP bonus awards can be paid in either restricted Common Stock or stock options (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Stock Awards&#8221;</font>).&#160;&#160;The Stock Awards vest 25% per year, over the first through fourth anniversaries from the date of grant, at which time 100% of all Stock Awards will be vested.&#160;&#160;The number of shares of restricted Common Stock and the number of shares underlying the stock options granted as Stock Awards were determined based upon the fair market value of the Common Stock on the date of the grant.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the stock options to be awarded as part of this plan was determined through use of the Black-Scholes valuation model.&#160;&#160;The Stock Awards granted pursuant to this plan were granted under the existing amended and restated 2005 Stock Incentive Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In March&#160;2009, the Board of Directors approved the awarding of approximately 1.1&#160;million shares to our employees under the LTIP for the 2008 calendar year.&#160;&#160;Due to the decline in our stock price, the Board of Directors suspended the LTIP in 2009.&#160;&#160;The LTIP has not yet been reinstated.&#160;&#160;However at the Board of Directors&#8217; discretion, bonus awards may be made in the form of restricted stock or stock options.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline">Stock Options</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We maintain a 2005 Stock Incentive Plan (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;2005 Plan&#8221;</font>) and authorized the issuance of up to approximately 5.8&#160;million shares of Common Stock pursuant to awards under the plan.&#160;&#160;In 2007, we also issued 250,000&#160;shares of restricted Common Stock to our executive officers outside of these plans.&#160;&#160;Approximately 1.7&#160;million (0.1&#160;million vested) stock options and 1.2&#160;million unvested restricted shares were outstanding at December&#160;31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Option awards outstanding have exercise prices ranging from $2.13 to $7.90 per share.&#160;&#160;In 2011 and 2010, respectively, 354,051 and 326,364&#160;shares of restricted Common Stock vested, of which 46,215 and 33,600&#160;shares were withheld by us to satisfy the employees&#8217; tax liability resulting from the vesting of these shares, as provided for in the restricted stock agreement, with the remaining shares being released to the employees and associated directors.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, we had approximately 2.1&#160;million shares of Common Stock available for future grant under the 2005 Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For stock options, we recorded $0.6&#160;million, $0.3&#160;million and $1.1&#160;million in expense (included on the Consolidated Statements of Operations in general and administrative expense) for the years ended December&#160;31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively, and an estimated $1.2&#160;million will be expensed over the remaining vesting period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, we consider whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&#160;&#160;The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income during the periods in which those temporary differences become deductible.&#160;&#160;We consider the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income and tax planning strategies in making this assessment.&#160;&#160;Based upon the level of historical taxable income and projections for future taxable income over the periods in which the deferred tax assets are deductible, we believe it is more likely than not that we will realize the benefits of these deductible differences net of a tax-adjusted $3.2&#160;million valuation allowance.&#160;&#160;The amount of the deferred tax assets considered realizable could be reduced in the future if estimates of future taxable income during the carryforward period are reduced.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ASC 740, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Income Taxes </font>(<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;ASC 740&#8221;</font>) prescribes a recognition threshold and a measurement attribute for the financial statement recognition and measurement of income tax positions taken or expected to be taken in an income tax return.&#160;&#160;For those benefits to be recognized, an income tax position must be more-likely-than-not to be sustained upon examination by taxing authorities.&#160;&#160;There was not a material impact on our operating results, financial position or cash flows as a result of the adoption of the provisions of ASC 740.&#160;&#160;A reconciliation of the beginning and ending amount of unrecognized income tax benefits is as follows:</font></div>

Our tax returns are subject to periodic audits by the various jurisdictions in which we operate.&#160; These audits can result in adjustments of taxes due or adjustments of the net operating loss carryforwards that are available to offset future taxable income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following table sets forth as of December&#160;31 for each of the preceding three years, the estimated future net cash flow from and Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Standardized Measure&#8221;</font>) of our proved reserves, which were prepared in accordance with the rules and regulations of the SEC and the Financial Accounting Standards Board.&#160;&#160;Future net cash flow represents future gross cash flow from the production and sale of proved reserves, net of crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids production costs (including production taxes, ad valorem taxes and operating expenses) and future development costs.&#160;&#160;The calculations used to produce the figures in this table are based on current cost and price factors at December&#160;31 for each year.&#160;&#160;Future income taxes were estimated using future cash inflows, future tax depletion expense on existing producing properties and available net operating loss carryforwards that existed at year-end for all years reported.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, the future pretax net cash flows from our proved oil and gas reserves are estimated to be less than the sum of the tax basis of the applicable producing properties and our available net operating loss (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;NOLs&#8221;</font>) carryforward; therefore, there was zero future tax benefit or expense at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;We believe it is more likely than not that all of our total available NOLs will be realized within the appropriate carryforward period.&#160;&#160;Our operations and all NOLs are attributable to our oil and gas assets.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure you that the proved reserves will all be developed within the periods used in the calculations or that those prices and costs will remain constant.&#160;&#160;A Standardized Measure is not required to be presented for interim financial presentation dates.</font></div>
